title: Uppercase Product Names
description:
Product names were entered in all lowercase. Use `UPPER()` to convert each name to **all capitals**.

**Table: products** — `id`, `name`, `category`

Return `id` and the formatted name aliased as `formatted_name`. Order by `id`.
schema_sql: CREATE TABLE products (id INT, name VARCHAR, category VARCHAR); INSERT INTO products VALUES (1,'apple iphone','electronics'),(2,'samsung galaxy','electronics'),(3,'coffee maker','appliances'),(4,'blender pro','appliances'),(5,'running shoes','footwear'),(6,'leather wallet','accessories');
solution_sql: SELECT id, UPPER(name) AS formatted_name FROM products ORDER BY id

test_cases.description: All 6 rows returned with names in uppercase

hints: UPPER(str) converts every character in the string to uppercase.
Alias the result as formatted_name so the column name is readable.
explanation: UPPER() is a single-argument string function. 'apple iphone' becomes 'APPLE IPHONE'. It is the standard way to normalize case for display or case-insensitive comparisons in engines that are case-sensitive.
